question.text: The Aravalli Long-Short Fund (Cat III AIF) currently has 980 non-accredited investors and 150 accredited investors. The manager wants to onboard 30 more investors, of whom 15 will be accredited. After onboarding, is the scheme compliant with the 1,000-investor cap?

answer.text: Yes — total investor count is 1,175 and well within cap
Yes — accredited investors are excluded from the count; non-accredited count becomes 980 + 15 = 995, still under 1,000
No — non-accredited count becomes 1,010, breaching the cap

explanation.text: The Logic: Only non-accredited investors count towards the 1,000 cap. Current non-accredited = 980. Adding 15 non-accredited (30 total - 15 AI) gives 995 — still below 1,000. Compliant. Accredited investors' count is irrelevant to this cap. The Trap: Option A ignores the cap; option C miscounts (995, not 1,010); option D wrongly includes AIs in the count. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B/C/D all test this exclusion. Easy to miss the AI carve-out.
